acceptance_criteria.criterion: The store list table renders all columns (Default, Label, ID, Path, Type, Projects, Repositories, Sync, Actions).
Type badges show "Git" (with ahead/behind when available) or "Folder".
Sync metadata displays as a badge with a hover popover showing provider, remote_path, and notes.
Path cells show truncated text with a click-to-copy button that copies the full path to clipboard.
The store modal opens in add mode (editable ID, Path, directory-mode toggle, Label) and edit mode (read-only ID and Path, editable Label).
The modal follows existing GUI modal patterns: fixed overlay, centered container, close-on-Escape, close-on-overlay-click, focus trapping.
Client-side validation rejects invalid slug IDs, non-absolute paths, and whitespace-only labels with inline error messages.
The "Use existing directory" toggle switches the API endpoint from addStore to importStore.
Import warnings from the API response are displayed as a non-blocking notification banner.
Mutating buttons are disabled with loading text during API round-trips.
Empty state is shown when no stores are configured, with an Add Store button.
All JavaScript is ES5-compatible — no arrow functions, const/let, template literals, or async/await.
The table is wrapped in .table-wrapper for horizontal scrolling.
Clicking Remove or Save in the Stores tab sends exactly one API call regardless of how many times the user has navigated away and back to the Stores tab.

comments.note: csPathCell() in config-stores.js uses max-width:280px on the cell container; the CSS uses overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis on .cs-path-text. On very narrow viewports (< 400px) the path may collapse entirely. A min-width guard on .cs-path-cell or a responsive media query could help, but is consistent with how other long-text columns behave in this SPA.

The sync popover (cs-sync-popover) uses position:absolute on td.cs-sync-cell. When the sync column is near the right viewport edge, the popover may overflow right. A future improvement could detect available space and flip the popover left. Not addressed here as no other popovers in the GUI have this guard either.

csWireEvents() re-registers a new 'click' delegated listener every time it is called (e.g., after csRefreshWithStores). Because the parent container (config-tab-content) is replaced via innerHTML on each re-render, the old listeners are garbage-collected — no actual leak. However, this pattern requires extra mental care when reading the code. A future improvement: attach the delegated listener only once after tab activation, using data attributes to prevent double-binding.

summary: Reviewed config-stores.js (690 lines), config.js, index.html, and styles.css. Implementation is well-structured, ES5-compliant, XSS-safe, and consistent with existing SPA patterns. Two blocking issues require Developer correction before PASS.

BLOCKING #1 — csWireEvents() listener accumulation: calling csWireEvents() inside an existing click handler (Reorder button, move buttons) adds a new listener on config-tab-content WITHOUT removing the previous one. The element persists across innerHTML replacements. After one reorder session, config-tab-content has 4+ listeners. Clicking Remove triggers N simultaneous confirm dialogs and N API.removeStore() calls. The Developer's 'GC reasoning' only holds when innerHTML is replaced before the re-wire — not in the inline-handler case.

BLOCKING #2 — Edit modal: empty label sends {} body. csValidateLabel('') returns '' (valid) because the guard is if (label && label.trim() === ''). csHandleModalSave sends body={} when label is empty (falsy), which fails UpdateStoreBodySchema (label: z.string(), required). For stores with no label, the Edit modal opens with empty field and Save always returns 'Save failed: Required'. The (optional) hint in the UI is misleading.
Fix-Forward: none — both issues require behavioral changes by Developer.
Documentation-Forward: modal close path does not restore focus to the trigger element (accessibility gap, WCAG 2.1 SC 3.2.2).

comments.note: BLOCKING #1 — csWireEvents() listener accumulation on config-tab-content. When the Reorder button click handler calls csWireEvents() (config-stores.js ~line 483), it runs inside listener #1 and adds listener #2 to the same element. config-tab-content is a persistent DOM element; innerHTML replacement removes child nodes but NOT event listeners registered directly on the element. After 1 reorder move + Done: 4 listeners. After 2 moves: 6 listeners. Clicking Remove triggers N confirm() dialogs and N API.removeStore() calls simultaneously. Fix: add var csClickHandler = null to module state; in csWireEvents(), call contentEl.removeEventListener('click', csClickHandler) before addEventListener, then store the reference: csClickHandler = function(e){...}; contentEl.addEventListener('click', csClickHandler). Also reset csClickHandler = null in the Stores tab cleanup block in config.js.

BLOCKING #2 — Edit modal: empty label field causes confusing API error for stores with no label. csValidateLabel('') passes (guard is if (label && ...) — falsy short-circuits). csHandleModalSave sends body={} when label is empty, but UpdateStoreBodySchema requires label: z.string() (not optional). For stores that were created without a label, the Edit modal opens with an empty field; clicking Save without adding a label always returns 'Save failed: Required'. The label field is labelled (optional) in the UI. Fix: in csHandleModalSave edit path, detect the no-change case and close cleanly — if (!label && !csFindStore(csModalStoreId).label) { csCloseModal(); return; } — OR change csValidateModalFields to reject empty label in edit mode with a helpful message.

[documentation-forward] csCloseModal() does not restore focus to the element that triggered the modal. WCAG 2.1 SC 3.2.2 requires focus to return to the opening control. Suggestion: add var csTriggerEl = null; set it to document.activeElement before inserting the modal in csRenderStoreModal(); call csTriggerEl.focus() in csCloseModal() after removing the overlay. This applies to both add and edit modes.

comments.note: BLOCKING #3 — Tab-switch cleanup in config.js (lines 94-99) nulls csClickHandler without calling removeEventListener('click', csClickHandler) first. config-tab-content is a persistent DOM element — replacing its innerHTML does NOT remove event listeners registered directly on the element. After the cleanup, csClickHandler = null, so when csWireEvents() runs on the next Stores tab visit, the 'if (csClickHandler)' guard is false and the stale listener is not removed. After N tab round-trips (Stores → other → Stores → other → Stores), N listeners accumulate, producing the same multi-confirm/multi-API-call behavior that BLOCKING #1 was supposed to eliminate. Fix: in the Stores cleanup block in config.js, call removeEventListener BEFORE nulling the reference: 'var _el = document.getElementById("config-tab-content"); if (_el && csClickHandler) _el.removeEventListener("click", csClickHandler);' — place this before 'csClickHandler = null'. Note: the renderConfigPage cleanup at line 58 is safe (app.innerHTML destroys the element entirely), so no change needed there.

Label field shows '(optional)' in both add and edit mode. In edit mode, clearing an existing label now shows a required-field error. The hint is misleading for stores that already have a label. Consider conditionally rendering the hint as '(optional)' in add mode only, or using mode-specific label text. Low priority — current behavior is correct, the copy is just slightly inconsistent.
